findings.text: Core name escaped formatter is available for building dump name components with sanitization. Callers provide a name accumulator plus a format and receive a status where zero means success.

Escaped formatting guarantees path safety for one component: slashes inside the newly added span become a benign mark, a component that would be exactly dot or double dot has its first character replaced, and an empty expansion is replaced by a single benign mark.

Executable identity expansion prefers the live executable file of the current address space. When unavailable it emits the short task name with an unknown path note, otherwise it resolves a full path in a bounded buffer and optionally trims to the final basename before escaped emission, releasing references on all paths.

Dump destination starts in one of three modes selected from the first pattern character: pipe mode, socket mode with a request submode when a second marker is present, or plain file mode. Only file and pipe continue to template expansion while socket returns after validation.

Socket destinations accept only absolute paths without spaces and without parent traversal, bounded below the unix path limit. Failures report a diagnostic and abort parsing with no further template processing.
Parent traversal detection treats exact double dot, leading traversal with slash, embedded slash enclosed traversal, and trailing slash traversal as matches using length aware tail comparison.

Pipe templates split arguments on whitespace before expansion so executable names containing spaces stay intact. Separators close the current argument with a terminator and record the next argument offset, while leading whitespace is ignored.

Template directives expand process and dump attributes including thread group and thread identifiers in namespace and global forms, credentials, dumpability, causing signal, wall time, host name under shared protection, short executable name with escaping, executable path in full or basename form, core size limit, originating cpu, and a fixed descriptor number for pipe mode. Doubled markers yield a literal marker and a trailing lone marker ends processing while unknown directives are ignored.

File names gain a dot plus thread group identifier suffix for compatibility only when the template lacked the thread group directive, the compatibility switch is enabled, and the destination is a plain file.

Descriptor based peer identification is only meaningful for pipe destinations and records the thread group leader reference, relying on exit ordering to keep the leader unreaped until the dumper exits; other modes skip this directive.

Group dump coordination moves from idle to group exit with a recorded code, then to collection where siblings are signalled and counted, then to rendezvous where the initiator waits for startup completion plus quiescence of each listed dumper thread, and finally to release where the exit code may gain a dump flag, shared state is cleared, and each waiter is detached with ordering and woken.

Thread zap and finish paths serialize group exit and shared dump state with the signal handler lock in interrupt masked form, while startup completion and per thread inactivity waits occur outside that lock.

Pipe helper rendezvous temporarily transfers one writer slot to a reader slot under pipe serialization, wakes input waiters and async listeners, sleeps until only the transient reader remains, then restores the original counts.
Pipe serialization is conditional: the pipe mutex is only acquired or released when the pipe currently has associated files, allowing lock free use otherwise.
Async input notification entry accepts a listener list, signal number and poll band. It performs a fast unsynchronized emptiness check before taking read copy update protection for the walk.

Async listener walk validates a per entry magic value and aborts with a diagnostic on mismatch, holds each entry lock while dereferencing its file and owner, suppresses unconfigured urgent notifications, delivers to valid owners, and follows the next link under read copy update.

Ownership delivery holds the ownership lock in interrupt masked form while snapshotting type and identifier, then uses read copy update protection to resolve a single task or iterate a group, releasing in reverse order.

Per task async delivery checks permission first, snapshots the configured signal number once, queues a real time notification carrying band and descriptor with poll code mangling and ambiguity avoidance for non poll signals, and falls back to a plain wake signal when queuing fails or no custom signal is configured.

Permission for async delivery requires the file owner identity to match the target saved or real identity or to be privileged, combined with a mandatory hook denial check, all evaluated under read copy update when reading target credentials.

Observed descriptor table layout comprises a capacity, a pointer array of file references, open and close on exec bitmaps, a secondary fullness bitmap, and a deferred free header. The files container holds a lock, table pointer plus embedded table, reference count, resize progress flag and resize wait queue.

Observed async ownership layout comprises an owner identifier plus type, custom signal number, owner and effective owner identities, and a protective lock. Each async entry holds a magic tag, its own lock, a file back pointer, a descriptor value and a next link.

Observed dump bookkeeping comprises a name accumulator with used length, buffer, mask, type, pipe limit and dumped flag; dump parameters with dumpability, signal info, cpu, target process reference and output file; and rendezvous state with startup completion, dumper list head and thread count.
Descriptor replacement installs a file at a chosen number after enforcing the open file limit and growing the table under lock. When given no file it closes the number instead.

Descriptor table growth serializes with the files lock, waits on a resize queue when another growth is in progress, enforces a global open limit, marks progress across the slow allocation, then wakes all waiters.

Table replacement allocates outside the lock, synchronizes readers when the table is shared, reinstalls the new table with ordered publication, defers the old table free except for the embedded case, and issues a write ordering barrier.
Table copy requires non shrinking capacity, duplicates existing file pointers, clears the new tail, and extends all three bitmaps to the new size preserving old bits.
Word count for descriptor bitmaps equals capacity divided by bits per machine word.
Secondary fullness bitmap storage size scales with capacity through a helper yielding element count times machine word size.

Descriptor table sizing rounds requested slots up to a power of two with a higher floor on narrow word builds, clamps down to the global open limit aligned to word size, rejects requests that would overflow signed range or exceed memory, and allocates header plus pointer array plus combined bitmap storage with staged cleanup on failure.

Descriptor close looks up the slot under lock with bounds and speculation protection, detaches the file and releases the slot, unlocks, then performs the file close outside the lock, reporting a bad descriptor when no file was present.

User mode dump helper setup optionally materializes a process file for the recorded target at a fixed low number, creates a pipe pair wiring the read end to standard input and retaining the write end in dump parameters, and clamps the helper core size limit to a minimal value.

Invalid async entry magic aborts the whole notification walk after logging, so one corrupt entry suppresses later listeners. Poll reason values outside the supported band range trigger a fatal trap rather than leaking stack.

Pattern expansion aborts on first output failure and rejects empty pipe or socket patterns, non absolute or overlong socket paths, and unknown destination kinds. File mode never records argument vectors.

Concurrent entry during group exit or ongoing exec causes the zap attempt to report retry, and a busy group reports busy. Only the first initiator clears pending signals, marks dump state and publishes the thread count.
